Ticket: INC-6604
Type: Data loss
Status: OPEN / UNRESOLVED
Detected: 2024-03-25 07:55 UTC
Detail: A migration run against the production Rails database (intended for the staging cluster, wrong Rails env var) dropped and recreated the `audit_events` table on the primary. Rows lost: approximately 1.4M audit events covering 87 customer accounts for the period Feb 12 – Mar 25.
Current state: Point-in-time restore initiated but blocked — WAL archiving was misconfigured since Feb 10, so restore is only possible to Feb 12. Data between Feb 12 and time of drop is unrecoverable so far. Vendor restore from nightly snapshot is being pursued for the remaining window; success unconfirmed.
Impact: 87 customers affected; audit trail incomplete. No further data loss possible (table locked).
Owner: dba-oncall + compliance. Escalated to legal for notification assessment.

Status page update — 2024-07-19 16:20 UTC: Between 15:40 and 16:05 UTC we performed an emergency kernel patch on two Elasticsearch nodes backing our search infrastructure. All customers were routed through read-replicas during the maintenance; there was no interruption or measurable degradation to search, dashboards, or saved reports. The patch is applied, the cluster is green, and the fix has been verified. No further action is required by customers. This incident is closed.

Postmortem — Data loss incident, March 22. A schema migration run against the primary customer database at 02:14 UTC included a destructive DROP COLUMN on the profiles table instead of the staging database. This affected all customers (~48,000 accounts), deleting avatar URLs, display names, and saved UI preferences. Game progress, transactions, and credentials were NOT affected (stored in separate tables). Restoration began at 02:50 UTC from point-in-time backups taken at 01:00 UTC; 74 minutes of writes made during that window were replayed from WAL archives. Full restoration completed at 05:31 UTC. We verified row counts and checksums across all shards, and ran a randomized spot-check with 500 customers via support outreach — all confirmed their profiles intact. Root cause: migration tooling applied to the wrong connection string. Fixes: staging/production namespace separation, a mandatory dry-run gate, and removal of interactive DDL from production access.

[Resolved] Internal alerting configuration issue — no customer impact

On 27 May, our on-call team identified and corrected a misconfiguration in an internal monitoring rule that was routing duplicate notifications for a single internal build system. The issue affected only internal tooling; no customer data, services, or features were involved at any point, and no customer accounts were affected (scope: internal only).

The fix was applied at 14:20 UTC and verified with a test alert, which routed correctly. This incident is closed. No further action required by customers.

on-call 11:47 UTC: reports endpoint slow for a subset of tenants (~15% of customers, mostly EU). p95 latency 9s vs normal 400ms. Suspect the new clickhouse sidecar added to the compose stack is starving the shared host of memory — container shows swap thrashing. Not user-down, pages still render. No fix yet; tried restarting the sidecar, no improvement. Next step: raise memory limit in the override file or move sidecar to dedicated host. Will keep monitoring. Ping me in #data-infra before touching this.

:white_check_mark: #inc-duperefunds — RESOLVED

Recap: On May 22 between 09:12–10:03 UTC, a concurrency bug in the refund controller (missing idempotency guard on retry) caused duplicate refund records for customers who hit 'retry' on a timed-out request. 312 customers were affected, with 409 duplicate refund entries totaling $58,441 in double-issued refunds.

Resolution: A database-level unique constraint plus idempotency-key enforcement was deployed at 14:40 UTC the same day. All 409 duplicate entries were reversed via batch job, verified reconciled against the payment processor ledger to the cent. Fix confirmed: 72 hours of monitoring with zero recurrences, and a regression test now covers the retry path. All affected customers received confirmation emails. Closing the incident — thanks everyone.

Ticket: INC-1877
Title: Internal compliance dashboard not refreshing
Status: RESOLVED (fix verified)
Opened: 2024-01-23 07:55 UTC | Resolved: 2024-01-23 09:20 UTC
Impact: The internal audit-trail dashboard showed stale data (last refresh 2024-01-22 23:00 UTC) for internal staff only. No external customers affected; the underlying audit event stream was unimpaired.
Scope: Internal tooling, ~40 employee users.
Root cause: A nightly Celery task that aggregates audit events into the dashboard's read store crashed on a KeyError introduced by a new event field; beat retries kept failing, so no aggregation ran overnight.
Fix: Patched the aggregation task to handle the new field (commit a91f2c), backfilled the missed 10 hours of events, and re-ran aggregation manually at 08:50 UTC. Verified dashboard freshness and event counts match source within 2 minutes.
Follow-up: add failure alerting for the nightly aggregation task (currently silent on failure), ticket TOOL-556.

[RESOLVED] Data incident — 12 Mar, affecting: ACME Retail (single tenant), status update 4 of 4. On 12 Mar at 11:38 UTC a misconfigured AOF rewrite on our analytics Redis cluster truncated a 6-hour window of ACME's event history (approx. 210,000 rows, 08:00-14:00 UTC). No other customer data was touched; ACME's data lives in a dedicated logical database. Resolution: we restored the affected keyspace from the 11:30 UTC RDB snapshot plus replayed AOF entries, recovering 99.6% of rows; the remaining ~850 rows were reconstructed from raw Kafka topics and verified against ACME's own counts. ACME's admin was notified in writing on 13 Mar. Final state: restoration complete and checksum-verified as of 15 Mar, 09:02 UTC.

Postmortem: Internal admin console outage, 2024-04-09
At 08:30 UTC the platform team merged a change to the GitHub Actions release workflow that pinned the wrong container tag for the admin console. The resulting deployment (build 2024.04.09.1) failed its readiness checks, leaving the internal admin console — used only by our 12 support engineers — completely unavailable; no customer-facing services were touched. Wrapping up #inc-2024-0611 — thanks all. Summary: starting ~09:05 UTC effectively everyone on the platform (all regions, ~3,100 tenants) saw sluggish performance: median API latency went from 180ms to ~2.4s and the web app threw intermittent errors on save. Status page update — 2024-03-18, 14:22 UTC: Between 02:10 and 04:55 UTC today, a misconfigured retention job on our event-log export pipeline permanently deleted Windows service event logs older than 6 hours for approximately 1,240 customers (about 9% of the account base). Postmortem: During the 2024-05-14 Terraform apply (run 8842, PR #1931), the firewall module briefly removed an ingress rule that a handful of our enterprise VPN users rely on — roughly 40 accounts were routed through a backup gateway for 11 minutes. No user-facing errors were observed: request success rates, p99 latency, and login completion metrics stayed flat throughout. Postmortem: Nightly Celery beat task 'billing.rollup_aggregates' failed silently on the staging worker pool after a Redis connection pool exhaustion event on Tuesday, April 9. The worker threw MaxRetriesExceededError for all 6 scheduled runs, but the downstream dashboard pulls the same numbers from a cache, so no customer saw stale or missing data — impact was confined to the internal finance reconciliation report, which was 6 hours behind until rerun. Fix: raised the pool size from 10 to 50 and added a task-level retry with backoff. Deployed Wednesday 10:14 UTC and verified by watching 3 consecutive successful nightly runs. Root cause was an unbounded fan-out in the rollup task spawning subtasks faster than workers drained them; a queue-depth alert now exists at 1,000 messages.

Ticket: SEC-5118
Title: Internal audit logs truncated — single-tenant deployment (Cobalt Freight)
Status: Resolved — verified
Impact: Security breach of audit data for one customer only. Between Feb 2 and Feb 9, the `auditlog` container in Cobalt Freight's dedicated stack wrote logs to an ephemeral volume declared in the compose file; container recreations during nightly restarts wiped the previous day's logs. Estimated 4,200 audit events lost (logins, permission changes). No other tenants or customer-facing data affected — product functionality was normal throughout.

Resolution: Corrected volume mapping, redeployed stack, and regenerated the missing audit entries from the reverse-proxy access logs where possible (3,900 of 4,200 events recovered; remaining 300 unrecoverable).
Verification: 48h of continuous audit writes confirmed intact across three container restarts; customer's compliance officer notified and confirmed receipt of recovered logs.
Follow-ups: add volume-mount check to tenant stack health tests (#5130).

RESOLVED — Security incident affecting user email preferences

Between March 7, 18:20 UTC and March 8, 04:55 UTC, a Terraform apply modified the permissions on our notification-service database, making the email-preferences table writable by an internal analytics job with a defective mapping. As a result, the notification opt-out settings of approximately 87,000 users (the majority of our customer base) were overwritten, causing opted-out users to receive marketing emails they had unsubscribed from. We have emailed a confirmation and a one-click re-preferences link to every affected user. Restores are confirmed complete and the incident is closed. A guardrail blocking database-permission changes outside approved change windows takes effect March 12.

Postmortem — Total checkout unavailability, 2–3 April

Summary: For 1 hour 53 minutes (17:04–18:57 UTC), checkout was unavailable to all customers, approximately 62,000 accounts, with an estimated 11,400 failed purchase attempts. The order service consumes payment-confirmation events from Kafka; a certificate rotation on the broker cluster caused all consumers in the `order-confirm` group to fail TLS handshake. A misconfiguration in the client's truststore reload logic (truststore path resolved relative to working directory, which differed in the new container image) meant consumers could not reconnect even after brokers presented valid certs. Because the order API blocks on confirmation events before returning, the whole checkout flow returned 503s.

Timeline (condensed): first alert at 17:09; root cause identified 17:52; emergency image rollback shipped 18:31; consumer group fully recovered and verified processing live traffic at 18:57.

Resolution and verification: the rollback restored processing; we then confirmed end-to-end by placing 200 synthetic test orders across all regions, all succeeded. Total order backlog drained by 19:40 with no lost payment events (reconciled against the payment provider's records — zero discrepancies).

Preventive actions: truststore path is now absolute and validated at container startup (deployed and verified in staging); broker cert rotation will be staged across brokers with a 24h soak between batches; checkout now degrades to async confirmation instead of hard-failing when the event stream is unreachable.

Postmortem: Search latency degradation, 2024-08-03.
From 01:15 to 05:47 UTC, search across our platform was slow or intermittently incomplete for effectively all customers: p95 query time climbed from 120ms to over 4 seconds and roughly 9% of queries returned partial results. The trigger was the nightly backup job, which at 01:00 began snapshotting the search cluster's data nodes over the same network path that handles inter-node replication. Backup traffic consumed ~70% of that link, replication lagged, and search queries started fanning out to stale or missing shards. The failure was mitigated first by pausing the backup run at 02:30 (which immediately halted the replication backlog) and completing it during the day over a dedicated path. The permanent fix, deployed and verified on 2024-08-05, moves backup traffic onto an isolated 10GbE interface and adds a replication-lag circuit breaker that automatically pauses backups when lag exceeds 5 seconds. We verified the fix with two consecutive nightly runs: latency stayed flat and zero partial results were recorded. No data was lost; the 1 August snapshot was completed successfully after rescheduling.

No customer data was affected.

Root cause: a malformed liveness probe config shipped in release 2024.10.29 caused kubelet to kill and restart every web-frontend pod within ~8 seconds of startup (events: 'Liveness probe failed: HTTP 500 on /healthz'), producing a restart loop across all 6 clusters. The probe path returned 500 because a required env var was absent from the new Helm values. Mitigation: release rollback via Helm at 14:38 UTC; all pods passed probes by 14:51 UTC and 100% of synthetic logins succeeded for the following two hours. Fix going forward: probe paths are now validated in CI against the rendered manifests, and the env var is set at the namespace level via a ConfigMap. Customer impact: dashboard unavailability for 49 minutes; API and data ingestion were unaffected.

Postmortem (draft) — Search latency degradation, June 3–5. Starting June 3 around 09:00 UTC, customers on the Growth and Scale plans began experiencing elevated search latencies: p95 rose from ~220ms to 1.8–3.4s, and roughly 8% of queries timed out entirely. An estimated 2,100 customers were affected; Enterprise-tier customers on dedicated clusters were not impacted. Initial investigation ruled out upstream provider issues; the trigger was traced to a GitHub Actions canary deploy that enabled a new index-compaction job, which competed for I/O with live query traffic during business hours. Mitigation attempted on June 4 (throttling the compaction job) reduced timeouts to ~3% but latencies remained elevated. We are preparing a full rollback of the compaction scheduler with off-peak-only execution and will confirm in a follow-up. This incident is ongoing; affected customers should expect intermittent slow searches until the fix is verified.

Postmortem: Unauthorized data exposure, September 12. A misconfigured grants change during a routine migration accidentally made the customer_notes table world-readable within the app database role. PostgreSQL server log records confirmed 6 anomalous queries accessing rows outside the requester's tenant during the window. We revoked the grants at 10:02, audited access logs to identify affected accounts, and notified the 41 customers individually within 24 hours. No evidence of data exfiltration outside the 6 logged queries. Fix verified by re-running permission tests across all tables. Status: Resolved. Action items: mandatory grants review in migration CI, tenant-isolation tests added.
